question: The speed of a boat in still water is 25 km/h. It takes 33(1)/(3)% more time to cover a certain distance in still water than to cover the same distance downstream. How much time (in hours) will the boat to go 75 km downstream?
solution:
**Given:**

Speed of boat in still water = 25 km/h

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance/Speed

**Calculation:**

Downstream speed = (25 + y)

Now, A/Q

Time take by boat in Still water = 33(1)/(3)% more time taken by boat in downstream 

d/25 = d/(25 + y) + (100/3)% of d/(25 + y)

⇒ d/25 = d[1/(25 + y) + (1/3) × 1/(25 + y)]

⇒ 1/25 = (3 + 1)/[3(25 + y)]

⇒ 1/25 = 4/(75 + 3y)

⇒ 75 + 3y = 25 × 4

⇒ 75 + 3y = 100 

⇒ 75 - 100 = -3y

⇒ -25 = -3y

⇒ y = 25/3

Time = 75/[25 + (25/3)]

⇒ 75/[(75 + 25)/3]

⇒ 75/[(100/3)]

⇒ (75 × 3)/100

⇒ 225/100 = 2.25

**∴ Time taken by boat in downstream is 2.25 hours **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Time taken by boat in Still water = {33}{1over3}% = {100over3} × {1over100} = 1over3 

Speed Ratio = 3 : 4

The boat speed in downstream = 25 × 4over3 

Time is taken by boat in downstream = {75}over{25×4over3}

⇒ {75×3}over{25×4} = 9over4 = 2.25 hr

**∴ Time taken by boat in downstream is 2.25 hr**
